prompt: A technician must replace a managed switch inside a control panel that also contains 480 V motor starter circuits. The panel disconnect has been opened and the technician has applied a personal lock and tag. What should the technician do next, before touching any conductors?

options.text: Disable PoE on the switch port from the network management console
Ask the control room operator to put the motor in manual mode on the HMI
Remove the lock briefly to confirm the disconnect handle moves freely
Test with a rated meter to verify a zero energy state

explanation: Lockout/tagout is not complete until the worker verifies isolation by testing for absence of voltage (try/test before touch). Putting the motor in manual mode on the HMI is a control action, not energy isolation. Removing the lock defeats the lockout. Disabling PoE on the switch port addresses only low-voltage network power, not the 480 V circuits in the panel.

prompt: A plant will install a wireless I/O gateway in an area classified as Class I, Division 1, where flammable gas can be present during normal operation. Which equipment requirement is most important for safety?

options.text: An extended operating temperature range of -40 to 70 degrees C
Certification for use in Class I, Division 1 hazardous locations
An IP67 ingress protection rating for dust and water
A NEMA 4X stainless-steel enclosure for corrosion resistance

explanation: Equipment in a Class I, Division 1 area must be certified for that hazardous location (for example explosion-proof or intrinsically safe) so it cannot ignite the flammable atmosphere. An IP67 rating covers only dust and water ingress. A NEMA 4X enclosure resists corrosion and hose-directed water but is not an explosion-proof rating. An extended temperature range addresses climate, not ignition risk.

prompt: An engineer must mount a cellular modem and antenna for a remote telemetry unit on top of a 30-meter water tower. Which control most directly addresses the primary hazard of this task?

options.text: A personal fall arrest system tied to a rated anchor
A lockout/tagout on the tower's booster pumps
A spectrum analyzer survey before installing the antenna
Arc-rated gloves and a face shield

explanation: Working at height creates a fall hazard, and a personal fall arrest system attached to a rated anchor is the direct control. Arc-rated gloves and a face shield protect against arc flash, not falls. A spectrum analyzer survey checks radio conditions and has no safety function. Locking out the booster pumps isolates hydraulic energy but does nothing about the fall risk.

prompt: Before a planned outage in which a team will update firmware on PLCs in a chemical processing unit, the supervisor wants to list each step of the work, identify the hazards of each step, and assign a control for each hazard. Which document should the supervisor prepare?

options.text: Root cause analysis
Failure mode and effects analysis
Job safety analysis
Business impact analysis

explanation: A job safety analysis (JSA) breaks a task into steps, identifies the hazards of each step and defines controls before the work starts. A business impact analysis measures the business effect of losing a process or system. A root cause analysis looks back at an event that already happened. A failure mode and effects analysis studies how equipment or components can fail, not the hazards of a worker's task steps.

prompt: A network technician must open an energized motor control center bucket to reach a communications module. The equipment's arc flash label lists the incident energy at the working distance. How should the technician select protective equipment?

options.text: Wear the plant's standard hard hat, safety glasses and high-visibility vest
Wear arc-rated PPE rated at or above the labeled incident energy
Wear chemical splash goggles and a rubber apron from the laboratory
Wear polyester coveralls with leather work gloves to resist sparks

explanation: Arc flash PPE is selected so that its arc rating meets or exceeds the incident energy determined by the arc flash risk assessment and shown on the label. General plant PPE such as a hard hat, glasses and vest is not arc-rated. Chemical splash goggles and an apron address chemical hazards, not thermal energy from an arc. Polyester can melt onto skin in an arc flash, so it is not suitable.

prompt: At the end of a shift during which a SCADA server was rebuilt, the maintenance lead gathers the team and the incoming shift supervisor to review work completed, abnormal conditions left in place and locks that remain applied. What type of safety meeting is this?

options.text: Outbrief
Pre-job briefing
Tabletop exercise
Incident postmortem

explanation: An outbrief happens at the end of the work to hand over status, open hazards and remaining isolations so the next crew is not surprised. A pre-job briefing happens before the work begins. A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based rehearsal of a hypothetical scenario. An incident postmortem reviews an incident after the fact and is not a routine shift handover.

prompt: An OT security analyst is choosing between two responses to suspected malware on a cooling-water control system. One response may stop the cooling pumps on a reactor. When weighing safety considerations, which should take the highest priority?

options.text: Maintaining the production rate committed to customers
Preserving forensic evidence on the affected controller
Preventing injury or loss of life
Avoiding physical damage to the pumps and reactor vessel

explanation: Protection of human life and prevention of injury is always the first safety consideration, ahead of environment and property. Preserving forensic evidence matters for the investigation but never outranks personnel safety. Avoiding damage to equipment protects property, which ranks below people. Maintaining production is a business objective and is the lowest priority when safety is at stake.

prompt: During an investigation, a technician must remove a pressure transmitter from a live steam line to inspect it for tampering. Which action best controls the pressure and temperature hazards?

options.text: Disconnect the 4-20 mA loop wiring and then unscrew the transmitter
Put the PLC in program mode so it stops reading the transmitter
Wear an arc-rated face shield while loosening the process fittings
Close the block valves, then bleed and verify zero pressure

explanation: Removing an instrument from a pressurized, high-temperature line requires isolating it with its block valves, venting the trapped pressure and confirming zero pressure first. Disconnecting the loop wiring removes the signal but leaves the steam pressure in place. Putting the PLC in program mode changes control logic execution, not the process line. An arc-rated face shield is for electrical arcs and does not prevent a release of steam.

prompt: A technician needs to replace an RTU inside the chlorine feed building at a water treatment plant. Which TWO precautions are appropriate before entering? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enter alone so that fewer people are exposed if a leak occurs
Rely on the chlorine residual value displayed on the HMI to judge air quality
Silence the building's chlorine gas alarm to prevent nuisance alarms during work
Check the atmosphere with a calibrated gas detector before entry
Review the safety data sheet and wear the specified respiratory and chemical PPE

explanation: Testing the atmosphere with a gas detector and following the safety data sheet's PPE requirements directly control the chemical hazard. Silencing the gas alarm removes a critical warning. Working alone in a chemical hazard area removes the ability to summon or provide rescue. The chlorine residual on the HMI measures dissolved chlorine in water, not chlorine gas concentration in the room's air.

prompt: The IT department wants to enroll the plant's HMI workstations in its standard monthly patch cycle, which automatically reboots machines overnight. The OT team objects. Which statement best explains the OT team's position?

options.text: OT systems are never connected to networks, so patching them provides no security benefit
OT prioritizes safe, continuous operation, so unplanned HMI reboots are unacceptable
OT systems prioritize data confidentiality, so patches must first be reviewed by the privacy office
OT vendors forbid all patching, so any patch voids the system's safety certification

explanation: In OT the priority is safety and availability of the physical process, so automatic reboots of operator HMIs can blind operators and must be scheduled and tested. Confidentiality is usually the lowest of the three priorities in OT, not the highest. Many OT systems are networked, so patching does provide benefit. Vendors generally publish lists of qualified patches rather than forbidding all patching.

prompt: At a water utility, operators adjust the speed of a raw-water pump from 60% to 80% on the HMI. Which field device directly changes the motor speed in response to that command?

options.text: Remote terminal unit
Protective relay
Variable frequency drive
Historian

explanation: A variable frequency drive controls an AC motor's speed by varying the frequency and voltage it supplies. A protective relay detects faults and trips breakers but does not set speed. A remote terminal unit gathers data and relays commands at remote sites but does not itself vary motor frequency. A historian stores process data and has no control function.

prompt: An electrical substation uses microprocessor-based protective relays that measure currents and voltages, trip breakers on faults and report data to the substation gateway using IEC 61850. What is the general term for these devices?

options.text: Intelligent electronic devices
Transient cyber assets
Operator workstations
Variable frequency drives

explanation: Microprocessor-based protection, metering and control devices in substations are called intelligent electronic devices (IEDs), and IEC 61850 is a common protocol for them. Variable frequency drives control motor speed. Operator workstations are PCs running HMI software. Transient cyber assets are portable devices such as laptops connected temporarily.

prompt: A natural gas pipeline company operates unattended compressor stations hundreds of kilometers from its control center. Each station has a ruggedized device that collects field I/O and exchanges data with the SCADA master over licensed radio. Which device type is this?

options.text: Manufacturing execution system
Engineering workstation
Historian
Remote terminal unit

explanation: A remote terminal unit (RTU) is built to interface with field I/O at remote sites and communicate with a SCADA master over long-distance links such as radio. A historian stores time-series process data. An engineering workstation is used to program and configure controllers. A manufacturing execution system manages production orders and tracking at site operations level.

prompt: During an assessment, the team must rank OT assets by how much damage an attacker could cause after compromising each one. Which asset is typically the highest-value target because it holds controller project files and software that can download new logic to PLCs?

options.text: Operator workstation
Historian
Engineering workstation
Network time server

explanation: The engineering workstation runs vendor programming software and stores project files, so an attacker who controls it can modify and download controller logic. An operator workstation runs the HMI for monitoring and supervisory commands but normally cannot reprogram controllers. A historian stores process data. A time server distributes time and cannot change control logic.

prompt: A refinery's process safety team insists that the safety instrumented system (SIS) remain independent of the distributed control system (DCS) and not be reachable from the DCS network. What is the main reason?

options.text: The SIS must still act if the DCS fails or is compromised
The SIS performs historian functions that would slow down DCS traffic
The SIS stores production recipes that must be protected from engineers
The SIS uses wireless protocols that interfere with DCS communications

explanation: An SIS is an independent protection layer that takes the process to a safe state when hazardous conditions occur, so it must not share failure or compromise paths with the basic process control system. Production recipes are managed in MES or batch systems, not the SIS. An SIS does not perform historian functions. SIS logic solvers are normally wired or use dedicated safety networks, not wireless links that interfere with the DCS.

prompt: Which description best fits a distributed control system (DCS) rather than a SCADA system?

options.text: Field devices at widely dispersed sites polled by a central master over long-distance, often low-bandwidth links
A single stand-alone PLC controlling one packaging machine with a local operator panel
A business application that schedules production orders and reports to the ERP system
Many controllers at one plant site, integrated under one vendor's system for continuous process control

explanation: A DCS typically controls a continuous process within one site, with controllers and operator stations integrated under one system and high-speed local networks. Polling widely dispersed sites over long-distance links describes SCADA. Scheduling production orders and reporting to ERP is the role of an MES. A single PLC with a local panel is a localized or stand-alone control system.

prompt: A food manufacturer wants a system that receives production orders from ERP, dispatches recipes to production lines, tracks work in progress and records batch genealogy. At which layer does this system belong and what is it called?

options.text: Level 0, a smart sensor network
Level 3, a manufacturing execution system
Level 1, a programmable logic controller
Level 2, a safety instrumented system

explanation: A manufacturing execution system (MES) sits at site operations (Purdue Level 3), between enterprise ERP and supervisory control, and handles orders, recipes, tracking and genealogy. A PLC at Level 1 executes control logic but does not manage orders. Level 0 contains sensors and actuators of the physical process. An SIS is a protection system that brings the process to a safe state and has nothing to do with orders.

prompt: A plant's water-quality analyzer runs on a stand-alone PC with no network connection. Technicians copy results off it weekly with a USB flash drive. Which statement about this system's security is most accurate?

options.text: Removable media is still an infection path, so media should be scanned and controlled
It cannot be infected because malware requires a network connection to spread
It should be connected to the corporate network so it can receive antivirus updates automatically
It needs no asset inventory entry because it is not connected to the control network

explanation: An isolated system can still be compromised through removable media, as Stuxnet's USB propagation demonstrated, so media must be scanned and controlled. Malware does not require a network connection to spread. Stand-alone systems still belong in the asset inventory. Connecting it to the corporate network would add new exposure rather than reduce risk.

prompt: A contractor arrives to commission a new packaging line and wants to connect a personal laptop with vendor configuration software to the line's control network for two days. How should this laptop be classified and handled?

options.text: As a historian that must be placed in the industrial DMZ
As an intelligent electronic device that must be registered with the substation gateway
As a transient device that must be authorized, scanned and recorded before connection
As a permanent engineering workstation that can bypass change management

explanation: A laptop connected temporarily to an OT network is a transient (portable) device, which must be authorized, checked for malware and tracked before and during connection. It is not a historian, which stores process data. Treating it as a permanent engineering workstation that bypasses change management would remove controls. It is not an IED, which is a substation protection or control device.

prompt: A tank level controller has been told to hold the level at 70%. The level transmitter currently reads 65%, and the controller is opening the inlet valve further. In this loop, what is the 65% reading?

options.text: Set point
Tag alias
Control output
Process variable

explanation: The process variable is the measured value of the condition being controlled, here the 65% level from the transmitter. The set point is the desired value, 70%. The control output is the signal the controller sends to the inlet valve. A tag alias is just an alternative name for a variable in the controller and is not a loop element.

prompt: A PLC is configured so that if it stops receiving heartbeat messages from the supervisory system for five seconds, it drives its outputs to a predefined safe state and raises an alarm. Which control concept does this describe?

options.text: Set point ramping
Watchdog
Retentive counter
Sequential function chart

explanation: A watchdog monitors for a periodic signal or heartbeat and triggers a defined action, such as a safe state, when it stops arriving. Set point ramping gradually changes a target value. A sequential function chart is a programming language for step-based sequences. A retentive counter counts events and keeps its value through power loss, but does not monitor communications.

prompt: A plant electrician with years of experience reading relay wiring schematics must review PLC logic for a conveyor interlock. Which IEC 61131-3 language represents logic as rungs of contacts and coils, making it most familiar to this electrician?

options.text: Function block diagram
Sequential function chart
Structured text
Ladder diagram

explanation: Ladder diagram draws logic as rungs with contacts and coils between two power rails, modeled on relay schematics. Structured text is a high-level textual language similar to Pascal. Function block diagram connects graphical function blocks with signal lines. Sequential function chart organizes a program into steps and transitions.

prompt: A control engineer must implement a complex flow calculation with loops, arrays and conditional statements in a PLC. Which IEC 61131-3 language is best suited to this kind of algorithm?

options.text: Structured text
Function block diagram
Ladder diagram
Sequential function chart

explanation: Structured text is a high-level textual language with loops, conditional statements and arrays, which suits complex calculations. Ladder diagram is best for discrete interlocks and becomes hard to read for math-heavy algorithms. Function block diagram is good for connecting reusable blocks such as PID loops but is cumbersome for loops and arrays. Sequential function chart organizes steps and transitions rather than detailed calculations.

prompt: A batch reactor program must move through fill, heat, hold, cool and drain phases, advancing to each phase only when a transition condition is satisfied. Which programming representation is designed for this structure?

options.text: Function block diagram
Ladder diagram
Sequential function chart
Instruction list

explanation: A sequential function chart (sequential function blocks) models a process as steps with transition conditions between them, which fits phased batch operations. Ladder diagram is oriented to continuous scanning of contact and coil logic. Instruction list is a low-level, assembly-like textual language. Function block diagram represents signal flow between blocks rather than step sequencing.

prompt: A motor must start only after an operator has held the start pushbutton continuously for three seconds; releasing the button early resets the delay. Which PLC instruction should the programmer use?

options.text: Up counter
On-delay timer
Retentive timer
Off-delay timer

explanation: An on-delay timer begins timing when its input becomes true and sets its output only after the preset time, resetting if the input goes false first. An off-delay timer delays turning an output off after its input goes false. An up counter counts transitions rather than measuring time. A retentive timer keeps its accumulated time when the input goes false, so releasing the button would not reset it.

prompt: A new pressure transmitter produces a 4-20 mA signal proportional to line pressure. During an integrity review, an analyst traces where its current value enters the PLC. To which type of I/O module does it connect?

options.text: Discrete input module
Discrete output module
Analog input module
Analog output module

explanation: A 4-20 mA transmitter produces a continuous signal, which is read by an analog input module and scaled to engineering units. A discrete input reads on/off states such as limit switches. Output modules send signals from the PLC to field devices: a discrete output drives on/off devices and an analog output drives devices such as control valve positioners.

prompt: An oil producer must connect SCADA to remote wellheads in a desert region with no cellular coverage, fiber or telephone lines. Which communication medium is most suitable?

options.text: IEEE 802.15.4 low-power mesh radio network
RS-232 serial cable run to each wellhead
Wired M-Bus networks used for utility meters
Very small aperture terminal (VSAT) links

explanation: Very small aperture terminal (VSAT) uses small satellite dishes to provide connectivity where no terrestrial infrastructure exists, at the cost of higher latency. IEEE 802.15.4 radios are low-power, short-range networks unsuited to long distances. M-Bus is a short-range network for reading utility meters. RS-232 supports only short point-to-point cable runs of roughly 15 meters.

prompt: A firewall between the HMI subnet and the PLC subnet must permit only the HMI's Modbus TCP polling of the PLCs. Which rule should the engineer create?

options.text: Allow TCP 44818 from any host to the PLCs
Allow TCP 502 from the HMI to the PLCs
Allow UDP 47808 from the HMI to the PLCs
Allow TCP 20000 from the PLCs to the HMI

explanation: Modbus TCP servers listen on TCP port 502, so the rule should allow TCP 502 from the HMI (client) to the PLCs (servers). UDP 47808 is the default for BACnet/IP. TCP 20000 is the registered DNP3 port and is in the wrong direction. TCP 44818 is used by EtherNet/IP explicit messaging, and allowing it from any host violates least privilege.

prompt: A water utility polls outstations with DNP3 and is concerned that an attacker on the network could inject unauthenticated control commands to open valves. Which protocol capability addresses this concern most directly?

options.text: DNP3 Secure Authentication
Increasing the integrity poll rate
Converting outstations to Modbus RTU
DNP3 unsolicited responses

explanation: DNP3 Secure Authentication, defined in IEEE 1815, adds challenge-response authentication of critical messages such as control commands. Unsolicited responses let outstations report events without being polled but add no authentication. Increasing the integrity poll rate changes how often data is refreshed. Modbus RTU has no authentication at all, so converting would not help.

prompt: A packet capture from a packaging line shows TCP sessions on port 44818 and cyclic UDP traffic on port 2222 between a controller and its remote I/O adapters. Which protocol is in use?

options.text: PROFINET
Data Highway Plus
Modbus TCP
EtherNet/IP carrying CIP

explanation: EtherNet/IP carries the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP), using TCP 44818 for explicit messaging and UDP 2222 for implicit, cyclic I/O. PROFINET real-time I/O runs directly over Ethernet frames rather than UDP 2222. Modbus TCP uses TCP 502. Data Highway Plus is a legacy proprietary token-passing network that does not run over TCP/IP.

prompt: A historian in the industrial DMZ collects data from an OPC DA server on the control network. The firewall team complains that the connection requires a wide range of dynamic ports. What should the engineer recommend?

options.text: Replace the firewall rule with a MAC address filter on the switch
Open all high-numbered TCP ports between the two hosts
Migrate to OPC UA and configure the SignAndEncrypt security mode
Tunnel OPC DA over Modbus TCP port 502

explanation: Classic OPC DA relies on Microsoft COM/DCOM, which negotiates dynamic ports, while OPC UA uses a single configurable TCP port (4840 by default) and supports certificate-based signing and encryption. Opening all high ports defeats the firewall. OPC DA cannot be tunneled over Modbus TCP. A switch MAC filter is not a substitute for a layer 3/4 firewall policy between zones.

prompt: A hospital's facilities team manages chillers, air handlers and lighting controllers that communicate over UDP port 47808 using an ASHRAE standard. Which protocol is this?

options.text: BACnet/IP
DNP3
KNX
EtherCAT

explanation: BACnet is the ASHRAE building automation standard, and BACnet/IP uses UDP 47808 by default. KNX is another building automation standard, but it is primarily twisted-pair based and its IP variant does not use 47808. DNP3 is a utility SCADA protocol. EtherCAT is a high-speed motion and I/O fieldbus for machines.

prompt: An engineer wants to use a router ACL to restrict real-time cyclic I/O between two PROFINET cells on different subnets, but discovers the ACL cannot see the traffic. Why?

options.text: PROFINET always encrypts its cyclic data, so ACLs cannot inspect it
Its real-time I/O frames have no IP header, so they are not routed
PROFINET real-time traffic is sent only over RS-485 serial links
PROFINET uses UDP port 502, which routers drop by default

explanation: PROFINET RT cyclic data is sent in Ethernet frames with its own EtherType and no IP layer, so it is not routed and IP ACLs cannot filter it; segmentation must happen at layer 2. PROFINET RT is not encrypted by default. Port 502 belongs to Modbus TCP, not PROFINET. PROFINET is an Ethernet protocol; serial RS-485 is used by its predecessor PROFIBUS DP.

prompt: A refinery is deploying WirelessHART transmitters for tank monitoring. Which IEEE standard defines the low-rate wireless physical and MAC layers on which WirelessHART is built?

options.text: IEEE 802.11
IEEE 802.1X
IEEE 802.3

explanation: WirelessHART, like ISA100.11a and Zigbee, is built on the IEEE 802.15.4 low-rate wireless personal area network radio. IEEE 802.11 is Wi-Fi, a higher-bandwidth wireless LAN. IEEE 802.3 defines wired Ethernet. IEEE 802.1X is a port-based network access control standard, not a radio specification.

prompt: Which TWO protocols are commonly carried over RS-485 serial networks in industrial plants? (Choose two.)

options.text: OPC UA
EtherCAT
PROFINET
PROFIBUS DP
Modbus RTU

explanation: Modbus RTU and PROFIBUS DP are serial fieldbus protocols that typically run over RS-485 multi-drop wiring. EtherCAT and PROFINET are Ethernet-based industrial protocols. OPC UA runs over TCP/IP or other modern transports and is not a serial fieldbus.

prompt: A plant's HMI runs a Windows version that is no longer supported, and the HMI vendor will not certify the application on a newer OS for another two years. Which approach best reduces risk in the meantime?

options.text: Remove the HMI from the asset inventory until it is upgraded
Isolate it in a restricted zone with application allowlisting and unused ports disabled
Upgrade the OS anyway and accept that the vendor will not support the application
Connect the HMI directly to the internet so it can receive emergency patches

explanation: For legacy systems that cannot be patched or upgraded, compensating controls such as segmentation, application allowlisting and port and service hardening reduce exposure. Upgrading without vendor certification risks breaking a critical application. Connecting it to the internet greatly increases exposure, and unsupported OSs do not receive regular patches. Removing it from inventory hides the risk rather than managing it.

prompt: A security team wants to install its standard EDR agent on every device, including line controllers that run a real-time operating system (RTOS). What is the best recommendation for the controllers?

options.text: Replace the RTOS with a commodity desktop OS so the agent can be installed
Exempt the controllers from all monitoring because RTOS devices cannot be attacked
Use passive network monitoring, since RTOS devices generally cannot run agents safely
Install the agent but configure it to scan only during shift changes

explanation: Embedded RTOS controllers generally cannot run general-purpose security agents, and anything that disturbs their timing can affect control, so passive network monitoring is the usual approach. Scanning during shift changes still requires an unsupported agent. Replacing an RTOS with a desktop OS would lose deterministic real-time behavior. RTOS devices can be attacked, so exempting them from monitoring is wrong.

prompt: An engineering team plans to consolidate twelve physical HMI and historian servers onto a single hypervisor cluster. Which new risk should the security architect emphasize?

options.text: Virtual machines cannot communicate using industrial protocols such as Modbus TCP
Virtual switches eliminate the need for any network segmentation between VMs
Virtualization prevents taking backups of the HMI configuration
The hypervisor and its management interface become a single point of compromise

explanation: Consolidation concentrates risk: whoever compromises the hypervisor or its management interface can affect every hosted VM, so management must be isolated and hardened. VMs can use industrial protocols normally. Virtual switching still requires segmentation, for example VLANs or virtual firewalls between VM groups. Virtualization usually makes backups easier through snapshots and image backups.

prompt: A utility deploys a software-defined network (SDN) in its substations so that flows between devices are centrally programmed and anything not explicitly defined is dropped. Which security consideration is most important for this design?

options.text: The SDN controller must be tightly protected, since it defines every permitted flow
SDN cannot carry IEC 61850 traffic, so protection traffic must use a separate network
SDN requires all devices to run the same operating system
SDN removes the need for an asset inventory because flows are discovered automatically

explanation: In SDN the controller holds the policy for every flow, so its compromise would let an attacker reprogram the network; it needs strong access control and isolation. SDN switches can forward IEC 61850 traffic. SDN does not require endpoints to share an OS. An accurate asset inventory is still needed to define the allowed flows.

prompt: A wind farm operator wants a turbine vendor's cloud service to analyze performance data, but does not want the cloud to be able to send commands to turbine controllers. Which design best meets this goal?

options.text: Place the turbine controllers directly in the vendor's public cloud tenant
Give the vendor a permanent VPN into the turbine control network
Allow the cloud service to poll the controllers over Modbus TCP through an inbound firewall rule
Use a local edge gateway that sends data outbound to the cloud through the DMZ

explanation: An edge gateway that sends data outbound only, through the DMZ, lets the cloud analyze data without a path to issue commands, keeping control on premises. A permanent VPN gives the vendor direct network access to controllers. Moving controllers into a public cloud tenant places control outside the plant. Inbound Modbus TCP polling from the cloud exposes an unauthenticated protocol that also allows writes.

prompt: Control engineers have started pasting PLC logic and network diagrams into a public generative AI chatbot to help troubleshoot. What is the most significant security concern?

options.text: Generative AI cannot interpret ladder logic, so the troubleshooting will fail
Sensitive design information is disclosed to an outside third party
Using the chatbot will automatically void the PLC's safety certification
The chatbot may change the PLC logic directly over the internet

explanation: Submitting PLC code and network diagrams to a public AI service discloses sensitive design and architecture information that could help an attacker and may be retained by the provider. A chatbot has no connection to the PLC and cannot change its logic. Whether the AI interprets the logic correctly is a quality issue, not the main security concern. Using a chatbot does not by itself change a controller's certification.

prompt: A plant uses a central integration server that translates data between PLC protocols, the historian, the MES and an MQTT broker. Which statement best describes the security significance of this middleware?

options.text: It can be ignored in risk assessments because it does not perform control functions
It should be exposed to the internet so that cloud services can reach it directly
It is a high-value target holding credentials for many systems
It replaces the need for a firewall between the control network and the MES

explanation: Middleware that bridges many systems aggregates connections and often credentials, so compromising it can give an attacker access across levels; it must be hardened and monitored. Not performing control does not make it low risk. Exposing it directly to the internet would create a path into the control environment. It does not replace boundary firewalls between zones.

prompt: A chemical company's board approves a statement that the company will tolerate no cyber risk that could plausibly cause a loss of containment, but will accept moderate risk of short production delays. What has the board defined?

options.text: Risk transfer
Risk register
Risk appetite
Residual risk

explanation: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk an organization is willing to pursue or accept in pursuit of its objectives, which is what the board's statement sets out. Residual risk is the risk remaining after controls are applied. A risk register is a record of identified risks and their treatments. Risk transfer shifts the financial impact of a risk to another party, for example an insurer.

prompt: A security policy requires accounts to lock after three failed logins. Operations warns that locking out the shared operator account on the control room HMI during a process upset could prevent operators from responding. What is the best balance of security and operations?

options.text: Exempt the HMI console from lockout, with physical access control and failed-login alerts
Remove all passwords from the HMI so that lockouts cannot occur
Apply the lockout policy anyway, because security policies cannot have exceptions
Allow only the security team to unlock the HMI during upsets

explanation: Where a control could interfere with safe operation, a documented exception with compensating controls (restricted physical access to the control room and alerting on failed logins) balances security and availability. Enforcing lockout regardless could prevent operators from responding to an upset. Removing all passwords removes authentication entirely. Making operators depend on the security team during an upset delays safety-critical actions.

prompt: A manufacturer's IT security team and plant engineering repeatedly disagree about who may approve changes to OT network controls. Which governance action best resolves this?

options.text: Ask the OT equipment vendor to make all security decisions for the plant
Create a cross-functional OT security governance body with clear decision rights
Let whichever team discovers a problem make the decision
Move all OT assets and change requests under the IT service desk's ticketing queue

explanation: Governance structures define who has authority and accountability, and a cross-functional body that includes engineering, operations, safety and IT security can make and escalate decisions consistently. Letting whoever finds a problem decide creates conflict and gaps. Treating OT as ordinary IT tickets ignores operational and safety expertise. Vendors advise but cannot be accountable for the asset owner's risk decisions.

prompt: A water utility documents how operators will keep treating and distributing water using local panels, manual valve operation and paper logs if the SCADA system is unavailable for several days. What type of plan is this?

options.text: Vulnerability management plan
Change management plan
Disaster recovery plan
Business continuity plan

explanation: A business continuity plan describes how essential operations continue during a disruption, including manual workarounds. A disaster recovery plan focuses on restoring the failed systems and data, such as rebuilding SCADA servers. A vulnerability management plan covers finding and remediating weaknesses. A change management plan governs how changes are proposed, tested and approved.

prompt: After ransomware encrypts the SCADA servers at a pipeline company, the team rebuilds them at an alternate site from offline backups and restores historian data, aiming to finish within the agreed recovery time objective. Which discipline does this activity belong to?

options.text: Penetration testing
Disaster recovery
Business impact analysis
Risk appetite definition

explanation: Disaster recovery covers restoring systems and data after a disruptive event within objectives such as the recovery time objective. Risk appetite definition is a governance decision about how much risk to accept. A business impact analysis is done beforehand to determine which processes are critical and set objectives. Penetration testing is a security assessment activity, not recovery.

prompt: A North American transmission utility operates assets that are part of the bulk electric system. Which set of cybersecurity requirements is mandatory and enforceable with financial penalties for this utility?

options.text: ISA/IEC 62443 series of consensus standards
ISO/IEC 27001 management system standard
NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection standards

explanation: NERC CIP standards are mandatory for bulk electric system entities in North America, and violations can bring financial penalties. ISA/IEC 62443 is a widely used consensus standard but is voluntary unless required by contract or local regulation. The NIST Cybersecurity Framework is voluntary guidance in the US. ISO/IEC 27001 is a voluntary certification standard for information security management systems.

prompt: An attacker alters a set point in a pharmaceutical plant, and several batches are produced outside specification and must be destroyed before release. Which category of business impact does this most directly represent?

options.text: Environmental
National security
Quality
Reputational

explanation: Producing product outside specification is a quality impact on the business, although it also has a cost. Reputational impact concerns public or customer perception, which did not occur because the batches never shipped. Environmental impact involves harm to air, water or land. National security impact concerns threats to a nation's defense or critical infrastructure at large.

prompt: A regional grid operator's leadership asks why its cybersecurity program must account for threats from foreign military intelligence services, given that the company itself has little of value to steal. Which driver best explains this?

options.text: National security
Contractual obligation
Quality impact
Reputational impact

explanation: Electric grids are critical infrastructure whose disruption affects public safety, the economy and defense, so they are targeted by nation-states regardless of the operator's own data, making national security a key driver. Quality impact concerns product specifications. Contractual obligations arise from agreements with customers or suppliers. Reputational impact is a business consequence, not the reason nation-states target the grid.

prompt: After an attack on a wastewater plant caused untreated water to be released into a river, the utility faced fines from its environmental regulator and lawsuits from downstream property owners. Which TWO drivers do these consequences illustrate? (Choose two.)

options.text: Inherited risk
Road map development
Business safety, environmental
Legal requirements and non-compliance
Benchmarking

explanation: A release of untreated sewage is an environmental business safety impact, and the regulator's fines and lawsuits show the legal and non-compliance consequences that drive security programs. Benchmarking compares a program against peers or standards. Road map development plans future improvements. Inherited risk is risk received from a provider or shared component, which is not described here.

prompt: A draft RACI chart for quarterly PLC firmware updates lists the controls engineering manager, the plant manager and the OT security lead all as Accountable. What should be corrected?

options.text: Accountable should be removed because Responsible already implies ownership
Each activity should have exactly one Accountable party
The OT security lead should be changed to Informed only
Every party listed should also be marked Responsible

explanation: In a RACI model each activity has exactly one Accountable party who owns the outcome and signs off, though several people can be Responsible, Consulted or Informed. Marking everyone Responsible does not fix the split accountability. Downgrading the security lead to Informed may exclude needed expertise and does not address the core problem. Accountable and Responsible are distinct roles, so Accountable cannot be dropped.

prompt: An electric cooperative wants to evaluate how mature its OT cybersecurity practices are across domains such as asset management, threat management and situational awareness, and express the results as maturity indicator levels. Which approach should it use?

options.text: A vulnerability scan of all substation devices and RTUs
A penetration test of the SCADA and substation networks
A Cybersecurity Capability Maturity Model (C2M2) assessment
A business impact analysis of each critical business process

explanation: The US Department of Energy's C2M2 is a maturity model that rates practices in domains such as asset management and situational awareness using maturity indicator levels. A penetration test checks exploitable weaknesses but does not measure program maturity. A business impact analysis measures the effects of disruptions on business processes. A vulnerability scan identifies technical flaws, not practice maturity.

prompt: The board of a water utility asks how the utility's OT security practices compare with those of similar utilities and with a recognized baseline such as CISA's Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals. Which program activity answers this question?

options.text: Benchmarking
Change approval
Root cause analysis
Road map development

explanation: Benchmarking compares an organization's practices or results against peers or a reference baseline. Road map development plans future improvements and usually follows benchmarking. Change approval is part of change management. Root cause analysis investigates why a specific event occurred.

prompt: A maturity assessment identified 40 gaps across a manufacturer's OT security program. Leadership wants a plan that sequences remediation over three years, starting with the gaps that affect the most critical production lines. What should the security manager produce?

options.text: A risk acceptance memo
A statement of work
A memorandum of understanding
A security road map

explanation: A security road map turns assessment results into a prioritized, time-phased plan of initiatives, which is what leadership asked for. A statement of work defines deliverables for one specific engagement. A risk acceptance memo documents a decision to tolerate a risk rather than plan remediation. A memorandum of understanding records a non-binding agreement between parties.

prompt: A manufacturer contracts a managed security service provider to monitor its OT network. The contract states that the provider must notify the plant within 30 minutes of detecting a high-severity alert and maintain 99.9% availability of the monitoring platform. What are these terms?

options.text: Memorandum of understanding clauses
Risk appetite statements
Standard operating procedures
Service-level agreement terms

explanation: A service-level agreement defines measurable service commitments such as notification times and availability, here with an external provider. A memorandum of understanding is generally a non-binding statement of intent, not measured service terms. Risk appetite statements describe how much risk the organization accepts. Standard operating procedures are internal step-by-step instructions.

prompt: Two neighboring municipal water utilities want to document their intent to lend each other control system engineers during a cyber incident. They want a written understanding of roles and expectations without creating a legally binding contract. Which document fits best?

options.text: Master service agreement
Statement of work
Memorandum of understanding
Service-level agreement

explanation: A memorandum of understanding documents shared intent, roles and expectations between parties and is typically not legally binding. A service-level agreement sets measurable commitments for a service. A master service agreement is a binding contract that sets general terms for future work. A statement of work defines specific deliverables under a contract.

prompt: A refinery already has a master service agreement with an integrator. It now needs the integrator to segment the crude unit network, with specified deliverables, milestones, acceptance criteria and a completion date. Which document should be issued under the MSA?

options.text: Memorandum of understanding
Statement of work
Acceptable use policy
Service-level agreement for help desk support

explanation: A statement of work issued under an MSA defines the specific scope, deliverables, milestones and acceptance criteria for a project. A memorandum of understanding is non-binding and lacks project detail. An acceptable use policy governs how users may use systems. A help desk SLA defines ongoing service levels, not a project's deliverables.

prompt: A utility is buying new protective relays and wants to reduce future security risk from the products themselves. Which TWO items should be included in the procurement requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: A clause that waives the utility's right to test firmware before installation
A requirement that relays use a single shared default password for easier maintenance
Evidence of product security certification, such as ISA/IEC 62443-4-2 component conformance
A software bill of materials and a vendor vulnerability disclosure and patch support commitment
A requirement that the vendor maintain permanent remote access to every relay

explanation: Procurement requirements should demand transparency and security assurance, such as an SBOM, a vulnerability disclosure and patch support commitment, and evidence of product certification like ISA/IEC 62443-4-2. Permanent vendor remote access increases exposure. Waiving the right to test firmware removes a key safeguard. A shared default password is a well-known weakness that procurement should prohibit.

prompt: The OT security manager must report a metric that shows whether the vulnerability management program is actually reducing risk. Which metric is most meaningful?

options.text: Percentage of severe vulnerabilities on critical assets addressed within target time
Total number of vulnerability scan reports generated and distributed each month
Count of emails sent to staff about patching
Number of security tools purchased during the year

explanation: A meaningful measure ties activity to risk reduction, such as the share of severe vulnerabilities on critical assets addressed within agreed timelines. The number of scan reports measures output, not outcome. Tool purchases measure spending rather than effectiveness. Counting awareness emails measures effort but not whether risk decreased.

prompt: A technician needs a document that lists, step by step, how to export and verify a backup of the logic in a specific model of PLC on Line 3. Which type of cybersecurity documentation is this?

options.text: Governance charter
Standard operating procedure
Policy
Standard

explanation: A standard operating procedure provides detailed, step-by-step instructions for performing a specific task. A policy states high-level management intent, such as requiring backups of controllers. A standard sets specific mandatory requirements, such as backup frequency and retention. A governance charter defines the authority and membership of a governing body.

prompt: A plant wants its control room operators to help detect cyber incidents. Which training approach is most effective for this audience?

options.text: Training on writing firewall rules for the industrial DMZ
Advanced malware reverse-engineering courses
Generic annual phishing training identical to what office staff receive
Role-based training on spotting and reporting abnormal HMI or process behavior

explanation: Role-based training tailored to operators' duties, such as noticing unexpected set point changes or HMI behavior and knowing how to report it, makes them effective detectors. Generic office phishing training does not address control room indicators. Malware reverse engineering is a specialist skill not needed by operators. Writing firewall rules is a network engineering task.

prompt: A utility's risk team gathers operators, engineers and security staff to walk through a specific situation: an attacker uses stolen VPN credentials to reach the SCADA HMI and opens breakers at three substations. The team works through the consequences and the safeguards at each step. What risk assessment method is being used?

options.text: Quantitative annualized loss calculation
Automated vulnerability scanning
Scenario-based risk assessment
Software composition analysis

explanation: A scenario-based assessment analyzes a defined, plausible attack or event sequence and its consequences step by step. A quantitative annualized loss calculation assigns monetary values and frequencies rather than walking through a scenario. Vulnerability scanning identifies technical weaknesses automatically. Software composition analysis inventories third-party components in software.

prompt: A compromise of a packaging line's controllers is estimated to cost $400,000 per occurrence (single loss expectancy) and is expected to occur once every four years. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
explanation: Annualized loss expectancy equals single loss expectancy multiplied by the annualized rate of occurrence: $400,000 x 0.25 = $100,000. $1,600,000 results from multiplying by four instead of one quarter. $400,000 is the single loss expectancy itself. $25,000 does not correspond to the correct formula.

prompt: The OT security team records each identified risk with a description, the affected assets, its likelihood and impact rating, an owner, the chosen treatment and a due date. Where is this information maintained?

options.text: Configuration management database
Risk register
Collection management framework
Change log

explanation: A risk register is the central record of identified risks, their ratings, owners and treatments. A configuration management database records configuration items and their attributes and relationships. A change log records changes made to systems. A collection management framework maps data sources available for detection and investigation.

prompt: A reliability engineering team lists each way a pressure control loop's components can fail, then scores each failure for severity, likelihood of occurrence and likelihood of detection to rank the failures by criticality. Which method is this?

options.text: Architecture review of network design
External network penetration test
Failure mode, effects and criticality analysis
Adversarial emulation of a threat group

explanation: Failure mode, effects and criticality analysis (FMECA) enumerates failure modes and ranks them by criticality, often using severity, occurrence and detection scores. A penetration test actively attempts to exploit weaknesses. Adversarial emulation reproduces a specific threat actor's behaviour. An architecture review evaluates design documents and network layouts for weaknesses.

prompt: A plant purchased replacement PLC CPU modules from an unfamiliar online reseller at a large discount. The OT security lead is concerned about counterfeit hardware or altered firmware. Which TWO actions best address this supply chain risk? (Choose two.)

options.text: Validate firmware versions and hashes against the manufacturer's published values before installation
Disable the modules' diagnostics so that tampered firmware cannot report errors
Rely on the reseller's online customer reviews to establish trust
Verify that the reseller is an authorized distributor and confirm the modules' provenance with the manufacturer
Install the modules immediately and monitor for problems afterward

explanation: Buying through authorized channels with confirmed provenance and validating firmware against the manufacturer's published hashes address counterfeit and tampered hardware and software. Installing first and monitoring later exposes production to risk before verification. Customer reviews say nothing about the authenticity of a specific shipment. Disabling diagnostics hides problems rather than detecting them.

prompt: A systems integrator will have remote access to a refinery's DCS for ongoing support. Before access is granted, the refinery wants to evaluate the integrator's own security practices, such as personnel vetting, credential handling and incident reporting. What is this activity?

options.text: Internal audit of the refinery's DCS
Business continuity test
Bare metal recovery
Third-party risk assessment

explanation: A third-party risk assessment evaluates the security practices of an outside party that will have access to or influence over the organization's systems; ISA/IEC 62443-2-4 defines requirements for such service providers. An internal audit reviews the organization's own controls. A business continuity test exercises continuity plans. Bare metal recovery is a restoration technique.

prompt: An engineering team is partitioning a new plant's control system into zones and conduits and assigning a target security level to each, based on a detailed risk assessment. Which ISA/IEC 62443 standard describes this process?

options.text: NIST SP 800-61
NIST SP 800-88

explanation: ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 covers security risk assessment for system design, including partitioning into zones and conduits and setting target security levels. ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 defines secure product development life cycle requirements for suppliers. NIST SP 800-61 is a guide to incident handling. NIST SP 800-88 covers media sanitization.

prompt: A gas utility needs a comprehensive catalog of security controls and guidance on tailoring them for OT systems. Which source best meets this need?

options.text: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)
The Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS knowledge base
NIST SP 800-53 with the SP 800-82r3 OT overlay

explanation: NIST SP 800-53 is a controls catalog, and NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 provides an OT overlay that tailors those controls for OT systems. MITRE ATT&CK for ICS is a knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques, not a controls catalog. The Diamond Model is an intrusion analysis framework. CVSS scores the severity of vulnerabilities.

prompt: A pipeline operator wants a red team to reproduce the documented tactics and techniques of a specific threat group known to target pipelines, so it can test whether its detection and response would catch them. Which assessment approach is this?

options.text: Tabletop review of policies
Qualitative risk assessment
Adversarial emulation of a threat group
Architecture review of network design

explanation: Adversarial emulation replicates the known behaviour of a specific threat actor to test detection and response against realistic tradecraft. An architecture review evaluates design documentation without simulating an attacker. A qualitative risk assessment rates risks using categories such as high, medium and low. A tabletop policy review is discussion-based and does not test technical detection.

prompt: A security consultant proposes running an active exploitation-based penetration test against the production DCS of a running chemical plant. What should the OT security lead require?

options.text: Use a test bed or a planned outage, under agreed rules of engagement
Approve the test without notifying operations so that the results are not biased
Allow the test only if it runs during peak production so that results are realistic
Cancel all testing, because OT systems can never be assessed

explanation: Active testing can crash or disrupt fragile OT devices, so it should be done against a representative test bed or during a planned outage, with operations involved and clear rules of engagement. Testing during peak production maximizes the safety and production impact if a device fails. Not notifying operations removes their ability to respond safely. OT systems can be assessed safely with the right precautions.

prompt: Two risks would have the same severe consequence: release of a toxic gas. In the first, the controlling PLC is reachable only from the control network. In the second, the PLC is reachable from the internet through a misconfigured cellular modem. Which risk variable is significantly higher for the second risk?

options.text: Recovery time objective
Likelihood
Impact
Asset value

explanation: Internet exposure makes exploitation far more probable, so the likelihood of the second risk is higher while the consequence is the same. Impact is identical because both lead to the same toxic gas release. The asset value of the PLC is the same in both cases. The recovery time objective is a continuity target, not a risk variable that changes with exposure.

prompt: After a site risk assessment, an auditor found a cellular modem connected to a remote RTU that the assessment never considered. The scope had been defined only as the plant's IP subnets. What should be done to prevent this in future assessments?

options.text: Limit future scopes to a single subnet so assessments finish faster and cost less
Scope assessments only from the vendor's documentation
Exclude RTUs from future assessments because they are field devices, not hosts
Scope by assets and every connection they use, including serial and cellular links

explanation: A sound scope is defined by the assets in the system and every communication path they use, including out-of-band links such as cellular modems, serial lines and wireless. Narrowing the scope further would miss more paths. RTUs are frequent entry points and must be included. Vendor documentation rarely reflects field modifications such as an added modem.

prompt: An internet search engine that indexes exposed devices shows that one of a utility's PLCs responds on TCP port 502 from the public internet. Which element of threat surface identification has the team discovered?

options.text: Threat actor capability
Inherited risk
Exposure
Control maturity indicator

explanation: An internet-reachable PLC service is an exposure, meaning part of the attack surface that adversaries can reach. Inherited risk comes from a shared or provided component outside the team's direct control. A control maturity indicator shows how well a control is implemented and managed. Threat actor capability describes the attacker, not the system's exposure.

prompt: A plant's HMIs authenticate users against the corporate Active Directory domain, which is managed by the IT department. A weakness in the corporate domain could therefore let an attacker log on to the HMIs. How should the OT risk assessment classify this?

options.text: Risk avoidance
Inherited risk
Residual risk after transfer
Control acceptance criteria

explanation: Inherited risk is risk that a system takes on from a shared service or provider it depends on, such as a corporate directory. Risk avoidance is a treatment decision to stop an activity. Residual risk after transfer describes what remains when some impact is shifted to another party such as an insurer. Control acceptance criteria define what a control must demonstrate to be accepted as effective.

prompt: After a plant deployed segmentation firewalls and application allowlisting on its HMIs, the risk team re-rated the threat of ransomware reaching the control network. The remaining rating is low but not zero. What is this remaining risk called, and what should happen to it?

options.text: Residual risk; it must be weighed against risk appetite and accepted by its owner
Inherent risk; it should be transferred to the equipment vendor under its support contract
Exposure; it should be escalated to law enforcement
Inherited risk; it should be removed from the risk register

explanation: Residual risk is what remains after controls are applied, and it must be compared with the risk appetite and formally accepted by an accountable owner or reduced further. Inherent risk is the level before controls, and vendors cannot simply be made to own it. Inherited risk comes from dependencies, and no risk should simply be deleted from the register. Exposure describes reachable attack surface, and law enforcement has no role in risk acceptance.

prompt: A legacy batch controller cannot be patched, and replacing it would cost far more than the estimated impact of the vulnerability. Existing compensating controls are already in place. The plant manager signs a documented decision to keep operating it as is and review it annually. Which risk disposition is this?

options.text: Accept
Avoid
Mitigate
Transfer

explanation: Formally deciding to tolerate a risk, with documented approval and periodic review, is risk acceptance. Transfer would shift the financial impact to another party such as an insurer. Avoidance would stop the risky activity, for example by retiring the controller. Mitigation would add new controls to reduce the risk, which is not the decision described.

prompt: A midstream company purchases a cyber insurance policy that covers business interruption losses from ransomware affecting its pipeline operations. Which risk disposition does this represent?

options.text: Mitigate
Transfer
Accept
Avoid

explanation: Buying insurance transfers the financial consequence of a risk to the insurer, although the operational and safety impact remains with the company. Avoiding would mean stopping the activity that creates the risk. Accepting would mean tolerating the loss without any shift. Mitigating would reduce the likelihood or impact with controls.

prompt: A vendor offers a feature that would allow operators to start and stop pumps from a public cloud dashboard. After reviewing the risk, the utility decides not to enable the feature at all. Which risk disposition is this?

options.text: Accept
Mitigate
Avoid
Transfer

explanation: Declining to adopt the activity that would create the risk is risk avoidance. Transfer would shift the impact to a third party. Acceptance would enable the feature and tolerate its risk. Mitigation would enable it with additional controls to reduce the risk.

prompt: A NERC-registered utility is visited by auditors from its Regional Entity, who review evidence of compliance with the CIP standards. Separately, the utility's own audit department reviews the OT access management process every quarter. Which statement correctly describes these activities?

options.text: The Regional Entity review is an internal audit because the utility pays for it
Both are external audits because they review OT systems
Both are internal audits because they occur on company premises
The Regional Entity review is external; the audit department review is internal

explanation: An audit performed by an outside body such as a Regional Entity is external, while one performed by the organization's own audit function is internal. Reviewing OT systems does not make both audits external. Where an audit happens does not determine its type. Who pays does not change the fact that the Regional Entity is independent of the utility.

prompt: The CISO must report OT cyber risk to the board of directors each quarter. Which reporting approach is most effective for this audience?

options.text: A raw export of every IDS alert generated across all sites during the quarter
Risks in business terms, such as safety, production and cost, with trends
Detailed firewall rule changes made in each zone during the quarter
A list of every open CVE identifier on every OT asset, sorted by CVSS score

explanation: Boards need risk reported in terms of business consequence, trend and the decisions or resources required. A raw IDS alert export is operational data with no context. A list of every CVE lacks prioritization and business meaning. Firewall rule changes are technical details relevant to engineers, not directors.

prompt: A high-rated OT risk has a remediation due date that passed two months ago, and the system owner has not responded to reminders. According to the program's risk monitoring process, what should the risk manager do next?

options.text: Transfer the risk to the IT department without discussion
Lower the risk rating so it no longer appears overdue
Close the risk in the register because the due date has passed
Escalate it to the next management level in the escalation path

explanation: Risk monitoring includes escalation criteria: overdue treatment of a high risk should be escalated to the management level with authority to act. Closing an untreated risk falsifies the register. Lowering a rating without justification hides the risk. Reassigning a risk to IT without agreement is not a valid transfer and does not address it.

prompt: A plant has deployed an OT network monitoring sensor to reduce the risk that attacks on its control network go undetected. Which risk disposition does deploying this control represent?

options.text: Mitigate
Avoid
Transfer
Accept

explanation: Adding a control to reduce likelihood or impact, here by improving detection, is risk mitigation. Avoidance would stop the activity that creates the risk. Acceptance would leave the risk as is without new controls. Transfer would shift its financial impact to another party.

prompt: A control engineer reads a vendor advisory describing a vulnerability in the firmware of the plant's I/O adapters. What is the first step in the change management process?

options.text: Ask the change advisory board for approval before writing anything down
Roll back the current firmware to an earlier version
Submit a change request describing the change, affected assets and reason
Download the firmware and install it on all adapters during the next shift

explanation: Change management starts with change identification: documenting what is proposed, which assets are affected and why. Installing the firmware immediately skips determination, testing and approval. The change board cannot approve a change that has not been documented. Rolling back to earlier firmware is itself an unreviewed change and may not address the vulnerability.

prompt: A vendor releases a security update for its HMI software. Before scheduling anything, the OT team confirms whether the vulnerability affects the plant's installed versions and configuration. Which part of change determination is this?

options.text: Approval
Rollback
Availability
Applicability

explanation: Applicability determines whether a change is relevant to the specific versions, configurations and assets in use. Availability concerns whether the system can be taken out of service and what downtime the change requires. Rollback is the plan for reversing the change. Approval is the authorization decision that comes later.

prompt: A firmware update for a compressor station controller requires the controller to restart. The team must determine when the controller can be taken out of service and what backup operating arrangements are needed. Which change determination factor is being evaluated?

options.text: Change identification
Availability
Applicability
Stakeholder communication

explanation: Availability determination considers the downtime a change requires and when the system can be taken offline without unacceptable impact. Applicability asks whether the change is relevant at all. Stakeholder communication informs affected parties. Change identification is the initial documentation of the proposed change.

prompt: Before deploying a new antivirus signature engine to HMI servers, the OT team wants assurance that it will not cause high CPU use or block HMI processes. What should the team do?

options.text: Test it on a staging system that mirrors the production HMI setup
Deploy it to all HMIs at once so problems are found quickly
Rely on the antivirus vendor's general compatibility statement for IT systems
Deploy it only to the backup HMI without testing and wait for operator feedback

explanation: Change testing on a representative staging or test system reveals performance and compatibility issues before production is affected. Deploying to all HMIs at once risks losing operator visibility everywhere. A general IT compatibility statement does not reflect the HMI vendor's software. Untested deployment to the backup HMI may leave the plant without a working failover.

prompt: A change request proposes downloading revised logic to a PLC that controls a kiln. Which item must be in place before the change is approved so the team can recover if the new logic misbehaves?

options.text: An updated network diagram of the corporate office and data center
A request to the ISAC for current threat intelligence on kilns
A tested rollback plan with a verified backup of the current program
A press release announcing the change

explanation: A rollback plan with a verified backup of the current program allows the team to restore the previous logic quickly if the change causes problems. A press release has no role in recovery. ISAC threat intelligence does not help reverse a logic change. A corporate office network diagram is unrelated to restoring the kiln PLC.

prompt: A change to firewall rules will alter how the historian sends production data to the MES that schedules Line 2. Which TWO stakeholders should be included in the change communication? (Choose two.)

options.text: The company's external auditor
The public relations department
The process owner responsible for Line 2 production
The system owner of the historian
The sector ISAC

explanation: The historian's system owner and the Line 2 process owner are directly affected and must understand and prepare for the change. The external auditor reviews controls periodically but is not a stakeholder in routine change communication. An ISAC shares threat information between organizations. Public relations has no role in an internal firewall change.

prompt: Which description best fits the change approval step in an OT change management process?

options.text: Approval is needed only for changes made to IT systems
Any engineer may approve their own change if they personally judge it to be low risk
Approval is given automatically once a change has been tested successfully
A change advisory board reviews risk, test results and rollback, then authorizes it

explanation: Change approval is a formal decision by a designated authority, often a change advisory board with operations, engineering and security input, after reviewing risk, testing and rollback plans. Self-approval removes independent review. Successful testing is an input to approval, not a substitute for it. OT changes need approval at least as much as IT changes because they can affect safety.

prompt: A weekly automated comparison shows that the logic in a filling-line PLC differs from the last approved version, and no change request exists for the difference. What should the OT team do?

options.text: Download the approved version immediately without telling operations
Update the approved baseline to match the current logic so the alert stops
Investigate it as a possible security incident and compare it with the approved version
Ignore the difference because the line is still running normally and nobody complained

explanation: An unauthorized change to controller logic may indicate tampering, so it should be investigated as a possible incident, with the differences analyzed. Updating the baseline would legitimize an unknown change. A line that appears normal may still contain malicious logic. Downloading logic without coordinating with operations could disrupt production and destroy evidence.

prompt: An operations superintendent asks why the change process requires department heads to be notified of a planned outage for a switch upgrade in the control network. What is the best reason?

options.text: Department heads can plan staffing and schedules around the outage
Department heads are responsible for writing the rollback plan
Department heads must sign the vendor's purchase order
Department heads must personally test the new switch firmware

explanation: Department heads control resources and schedules, so informing them lets them allocate staff and plan around the outage in their areas. Firmware testing is done by engineering. Purchasing is a procurement activity separate from change communication. The rollback plan is written by the technical team performing the change.

prompt: A threat analyst reviews vendor security advisories, conference presentations and public social media posts by hacktivists to learn about threats to water utilities. Which intelligence type is this?

options.text: Imagery intelligence
Open-source intelligence
Human intelligence
Signals intelligence

explanation: Open-source intelligence (OSINT) comes from publicly available information such as advisories, presentations and social media. Signals intelligence comes from intercepted communications or electronic signals. Human intelligence is gathered from people through direct interaction. Imagery intelligence comes from photographs or satellite imagery.

prompt: During a sector meeting, an engineer from a peer utility privately describes suspicious remote access attempts they experienced. The OT security team records the details as intelligence. Which intelligence type is this?

options.text: Open-source intelligence
Measurement and signature intelligence
Human intelligence
Signals intelligence

explanation: Human intelligence (HUMINT) is information gathered from people through conversation or other direct contact. Measurement and signature intelligence comes from technical sensor data. Signals intelligence comes from intercepted signals. Open-source intelligence is publicly available, whereas this was shared privately.

prompt: A national agency intercepts and analyzes an adversary's command-and-control communications to learn which energy companies it is targeting. Which intelligence type is this?

options.text: Signals intelligence
Open-source intelligence
Imagery intelligence
Human intelligence

explanation: Signals intelligence (SIGINT) is derived from intercepting and analyzing communications and other electronic signals. Imagery intelligence comes from photographs or satellite images. Human intelligence comes from human sources. Open-source intelligence uses publicly available material, not intercepted communications.

prompt: Analysts examine thermal, acoustic and spectral data captured by technical sensors to identify which type of turbines are operating at a foreign facility. Which intelligence type is this?

options.text: Human intelligence
Open-source intelligence
Signals intelligence
Measurement and signature intelligence

explanation: Measurement and signature intelligence (MASINT) is derived from quantitative analysis of data from technical sensors, such as thermal, acoustic or spectral signatures. Human intelligence comes from people. Open-source intelligence comes from public sources. Signals intelligence concerns intercepted communications and electronic emissions rather than physical signatures.

prompt: A threat intelligence provider uses commercial satellite photographs to show that a new substation and control building have been built near a contested border. Which intelligence type is this?

options.text: Human intelligence
Imagery intelligence
Measurement and signature intelligence
Signals intelligence

explanation: Imagery intelligence (IMINT) is derived from photographs and satellite or aerial imagery. Signals intelligence comes from intercepted communications. Human intelligence comes from human sources. Measurement and signature intelligence analyzes sensor data such as acoustic or thermal signatures rather than visual imagery.

prompt: An analyst using the Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis maps an intrusion in which a threat group used a custom ICS malware family delivered from a set of rented virtual private servers against a utility. In the model, what do the rented servers represent?

options.text: Victim
Capability
Infrastructure
Adversary

explanation: The Diamond Model's four vertices are adversary, capability, infrastructure and victim, and the servers used to deliver and control the attack are infrastructure. The adversary is the threat group. The capability is the malware and tradecraft. The victim is the targeted utility.

prompt: A threat intelligence team has analyzed collected data and written a report on a new campaign targeting PLCs. In the intelligence life cycle, what is the next step?

options.text: Collection
Planning and direction
Processing
Dissemination

explanation: After analysis and production, intelligence is disseminated to the consumers who need it, such as the SOC and plant leaders, followed by feedback. Planning and direction sets requirements at the start of the cycle. Collection gathers raw data. Processing converts raw data into a usable form before analysis.

prompt: During an intrusion, an adversary suppresses alarm messages to the HMI and modifies the safety instrumented system logic so that it will not trip. Under which MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactic do these actions fall?

options.text: Initial Access
Inhibit Response Function
Discovery
Collection

explanation: Inhibit Response Function covers techniques that stop safety, protection and operator response functions from reacting, such as alarm suppression and tampering with safety logic. Initial Access covers how the adversary first gets into the environment. Discovery covers learning about the environment. Collection covers gathering data of interest.

prompt: An adversary sends unauthorized command messages to field controllers and changes process parameters so that a valve opens beyond its normal range. Which MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactic describes this goal?

options.text: Impair Process Control
Lateral Movement
